title: The Hooded Confessor
text: A hooded confessor sits in the cathedral's darkest booth and hears the city's sins for nothing, day and night, and never seems to tire. He remembers every one. He has begun to write them down, in a great black book, in a hand that is very neat.

options.label: Let him hear the city's sins.

outcomes.text: The city sleeps easier, unburdened, and the black book grows.
Pages of his book turn up nailed to doors. One carries a House's name, and a sin the House thought buried.
The book is a ledger of every House's secrets. Each House takes its own page, and reads the others'.
There is no book. There was never a confessor. The booth smells of wet earth, and every House's sins are whispered in its halls that night.
He leaves in spring, heavy with secrets, by the road toward the Gate. Whatever waits there will read them.
